solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Endless fruit, gold and diamonds bring cheer

indicators.note: endless says the fruit word loses its final letter

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A gift of fruit, gold and jewels is enough to lift anyone's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud is to clap and cheer, giving a performer a cheer of approval.

clue.text: A strange charm I heard in Ethiopia

indicators.note: strange says the letters of these words are oddly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder of the anagram

explanation.surface: A traveller in Ethiopia catches an exotic, charming sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard in Ethiopia' points to a language spoken there; 'strange' looks like a description of the charm but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Amharic is the official language of Ethiopia, so it is the tongue heard spoken there.

clue.text: Explain how to vote to an audience

explanation.surface: A canvasser instructs a crowd on how to mark a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words, 'put a cross' is how a British voter marks a ballot paper; 'to an audience' rounds off the sense of putting a point over to listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something across is an idiom for communicating or explaining it successfully.

clue.text: Arsenic layer, pale in colour

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
a hen is a layer of eggs

explanation.surface: A coating of arsenic leaves something looking pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a stratum, but here it is something that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen is a synonym of pallid, the grey colour of ash.

clue.text: Stress in the evening rush hour

explanation.surface: Commuting in the evening rush is stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links stress to rush hour; really 'stress' is one sense and the commute home by car is the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a point home is an idiom for emphasising it, and commuters drive home in the evening.

clue.text: Cheers below deck?

explanation.surface: Sailors raise a toast down in the ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: A toast before drinking is one sense; literally going through the hatch takes you beneath a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a drinking toast, and literally it means passing through a ship's hatchway to the lower deck.

clue.text: Fighting ends in grave — a soldier's lament

indicators.note: in says the last letter of the first word is placed inside the synonym for grave

parts.note: a grave situation is a dire one

indicators.note: ends picks out the closing letter of the word fighting

explanation.surface: When the fighting is over, a soldier's lament is sung at a graveside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' is not a burial place but an adjective meaning serious, giving DIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song of mourning, such as one played at a soldier's funeral.

clue.text: Heading 270°, we tied up around central Boston

indicators.note: around says the first two pieces are wrapped about the middle letters

parts.note: taken as written
bound means tied up

indicators.note: central picks the middle pair of letters from the city name

explanation.surface: A traveller heading due west ties up their luggage near the centre of Boston.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' takes the middle two letters of BOSTON; 'around' sets the other two pieces either side of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass bearing of 270 degrees points due west, so travelling that way is going west.

clue.text: Intricate organ, perhaps the abode of monsters once

indicators.note: perhaps says these letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder of the anagram

explanation.surface: A complicated organ may be where monsters once lived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intricate' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'perhaps' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Old maps marked unexplored land as unknown territory and decorated it with sea serpents and monsters.

clue.text: Eeyore's messy pigstye, you might say

indicators.note: messy says the letters of the donkey's name are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written with its s, the fodder of the anagram

explanation.surface: The gloomy donkey Eeyore keeps a messy pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the possessive s is a letter of the fodder. 'pigstye' runs together pigsty and eye-stye, a punning picture of an ugly sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsightly mess is something offensive to the eye, as a pigsty would be.

clue.text: See 5
Popular book, available for use

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A best-selling book is ready for borrowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is a verb here, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held back ready to be drawn on when needed is kept in reserve.

clue.text: Never once managed to meet again

indicators.note: managed says the letters are handled and arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder of the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone complains that they never once managed to get together again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to assemble once more after a break, as a committee does.

clue.text: Order to vote against the party

explanation.surface: A ballot instruction tells members to oppose the party.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'be a no', an instruction to vote against; a beano is also a British slang word for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is British slang for a festive celebration or knees-up.

clue.text: Small bulb of a forage plant, cut down

indicators.note: cut down says the plant's name is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: clover is grown as fodder for livestock

explanation.surface: A farmer cuts down a forage crop and finds a small bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove is one of the small segments that make up a bulb of garlic.

clue.text: Medically speaking, it determines only superficial beauty

definitions.text: Medically speaking, it determines only superficial beauty

parts.words: Medically speaking, it determines only superficial beauty
parts.note: beauty is only skin deep, and the medical name for the outer layer of skin is what fixes that surface appeal

explanation.surface: A doctor explains that good looks are only skin deep.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outermost layer of the skin, so it is where superficial looks lie.

clue.text: "Nosy" virus to be modified

indicators.note: modified says the letters of the preceding words are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder of the anagram

explanation.surface: A virus is about to mutate into an intrusive strain.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'Nosy' make it look like a nickname for the virus; it is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being obtrusive means pushing in where not wanted, much like being prying.

clue.text: Show disapproval or maybe barge into teacher's office

parts.note: tut is a click of the tongue to show disapproval
taken as written
a barge is one kind of ship

explanation.surface: Someone tuts or barges into a teacher's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barge into' reads as a verb of rudeness; 'barge' is the boat, and 'into' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorship is the post or office of a tutor, a kind of teacher.

clue.text: See 7
Annoying pet finally interrupts Mum after exercise

indicators.note: after says the remaining letters follow the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: PE is physical exercise in school

indicators.note: interrupts says a letter breaks into the word for mum

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keeping mum

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of pet

explanation.surface: An irritating pet butts in while Mum is recovering from a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but the adjective meaning quiet, SILENT; T goes inside after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilent is used figuratively for something irritating or troublesome, like a pest.

clue.text: Girls positioned on each knee

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Two girls are each perched on someone's knee.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'Girls', supplies two names; 'positioned' just links them to a definition describing the bone's place on the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, the bone that sits on the front of every knee.

clue.text: Transfer agreement involving Chelsea primarily

indicators.note: involving says the deal word contains a letter

parts.note: a deal is an agreement

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the club name

explanation.surface: A football transfer deal involving Chelsea Football Club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transfer' suggests a football player move; it is a decorative sticker. Chelsea is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A decal is a design transferred from paper onto a surface, so it is a transfer.

clue.text: One long retired told tales about Lincoln

indicators.note: about says the word for fibbed goes round the president's name

parts.note: lied means told tales or fibbed
Abe is Abraham Lincoln's nickname

explanation.surface: A long-retired person told stories about Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' means gone to bed, not stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-abed is someone who stays in bed late, having turned in for a long time.

clue.text: Stretch of water seems rather short

indicators.note: Stretch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stretch of water looks fairly narrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse describes something brief and curt, using few words.

clue.text: Old scout car

explanation.surface: An elderly Scout drives a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A Rover was an older Scout in the British Scouting movement, and Rover is a British car make.
explanation.definitionFit: Rover Scouts were the senior branch of Scouting, and Rover is a British car brand.

clue.text: Shark and dog go after meat, mostly

indicators.note: go after says the dog breed follows the shortened meat
mostly says the meat loses its last letter

parts.note: pork is meat
a beagle is a dog breed

explanation.surface: A shark and a dog chase after a hunk of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The porbeagle is a mackerel shark of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Floral segment upturned in umbellate plants

indicators.note: upturned says the hidden letters are read backwards
segment says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A segment of a flower is turned upwards on umbelliferous plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floral segment' reads as one phrase for the answer, but 'Floral' alone is the definition and 'segment' signals the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is a part of a flower, so the adjective names it loosely as a floral thing.

clue.text: Letters are said to make you better

indicators.note: are said says the letters are spoken out loud

parts.note: the letters X and L, spoken, give the sound

explanation.surface: Reciting letters supposedly improves you.
explanation.walkthrough: XL spoken aloud is 'ex-el'.
explanation.definitionFit: To better something is to surpass it, which is what excelling means.

clue.text: There's nothing to equal romantic marriage

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring
a match is an equal

explanation.surface: Nothing compares with a marriage built on romance.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, a score of zero is called love.
explanation.definitionFit: A love match is a marriage made for affection rather than money or status.

clue.text: Increase cost initially to member

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of cost

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A rise in costs is passed on first to members.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that climb are rising, so to climb is to go up.

clue.text: Roseola treated with chemical spray

indicators.note: treated says the illness name is worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder of the anagram

explanation.surface: A rash of roseola is treated with a chemical spray.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised can releasing a fine mist of chemicals.

clue.text: Hornless animal that's cut back on fat

indicators.note: back says the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A hornless beast has its fat trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut back' looks like one phrase meaning trimmed; split it, LOP reversed, and 'on' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A pollard is an animal that has lost or shed its horns, such as a polled ox.
